This represents the sum of population across all 1km grid cells whose centroid point falls within a 5km radius of any of the 15 GENERAL stations, with each grid cell counted only once regardless of how many stations are nearby.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sqlalchemy import text

# Get all GENERAL station coordinates
query = text("""
SELECT id, name_en, ST_X(coordinate::geometry) as lon, ST_Y(coordinate::geometry) as lat
FROM air_quality_station
WHERE station_type = 'GENERAL'
""")
general_stations = pd.read_sql(query, engine)
print(f"Number of GENERAL stations: {len(general_stations)}")
print(general_stations[['name_en', 'lon', 'lat']].to_string())

# Haversine function
def haversine_np(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2):
    lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2 = map(np.radians, [lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2])
    dlon = lon2 - lon1
    dlat = lat2 - lat1
    a = np.sin(dlat/2)**2 + np.cos(lat1) * np.cos(lat2) * np.sin(dlon/2)**2
    c = 2 * np.arcsin(np.sqrt(a))
    return 6371000 * c  # meters
